notes: Port: 3389/tcp+udp. rdp-sec-check needs Perl Encoding::BER (install via cpan).

recommended.note: Hijack an existing session with SYSTEM.

name: RDP - Enumeration & Connect
description: Scan RDP with the rdp* NSE scripts, assess its security config with rdp-sec-check, then connect with xfreerdp.

defense.why_it_works: Adversaries scan for open ports and running services on network hosts to identify attack surface and potential exploitation targets. Tools like netcat, nmap, and service-specific clients probe for banner information that reveals software versions, which can then be matched against known vulnerabilities.
defense.impact: RDP version, NLA status, and certificate details - enabling CVE matching (e.g. BlueKeep) and spraying decisions.
defense.detection: Monitor for processes performing network enumeration by correlating process creation, socket connections, and sequential destination IP probing within a time window. Unusual port scanning patterns or banner-grabbing activity from internal hosts can indicate post-compromise discovery.
defense.artifacts: Connection attempts in the RDP/Security logs (Event 4625 on failed auth); traffic to 3389.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=network dest_port=3389
| stats count dc(dest_ip) as hosts by src_ip, bin(_time, 1m)
| where count>10 OR hosts>5
defense.sentinel_kql:
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where RemotePort == 3389
| summarize probes=count(), hosts=dcount(RemoteIP) by LocalIP, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where probes > 10 or hosts > 5
| sort by probes desc
// RDP security-layer/NLA enumeration (rdp-sec-check / nmap rdp-* scripts)
defense.prevention: Close unnecessary ports and services to prevent risk of discovery and potential exploitation. Use network intrusion detection/prevention systems to detect and prevent remote service scans. Ensure proper network segmentation to protect critical servers and devices.
defense.misconfiguration: RDP (TCP 3389) is exposed to the internet or internal networks without NLA (Network Level Authentication), allowing unauthenticated brute force at the login screen. Session hijacking exploits the Windows tscon.exe utility which can reconnect disconnected sessions without a password when run as SYSTEM.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# RDP without NLA - authentication happens INSIDE the session (post-connection):
# Attacker can reach the Windows login screen without any prior auth
# Enables brute force + BlueKeep/DejaBlue exploitation

# Disconnected sessions hijackable:
# > query session  -> shows disconnected admin session
# > tscon <ID> /dest:console  (as SYSTEM) -> hijacks session without password
defense.secure_config:
# Enable NLA:
# Group Policy: Computer Config -> Admin Templates -> Windows Components -> RDS
#   'Require NLA' = Enabled
# Registry: HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Control\Terminal Server\WinStations\RDP-Tcp
#   UserAuthentication = 1

# Restrict RDP access:
New-NetFirewallRule -Name 'RDP Allow' -Protocol TCP -LocalPort 3389 \
    -RemoteAddress 10.10.1.0/24 -Action Allow
New-NetFirewallRule -Name 'RDP Block' -Protocol TCP -LocalPort 3389 -Action Block

# Prevent session hijacking:
# Enable RDP session timeouts + automatic logoff for disconnected sessions
# GPO: Disconnect + log off after 15 minutes idle
defense.evasion: WinRM with valid creds looks like normal management; avoid dropping tools - run built-ins over the session; clear PSReadline history on the remote host after.

explain:
Enumerates an RDP service and its security settings:
  nmap -sV -sC <ip> -p3389   version + default scripts on RDP
  --script rdp*              run the RDP-specific NSE scripts
Reports the RDP config; rdp-sec-check.pl then flags weak security layers (e.g. no NLA, downgrade to RDP Security), and xfreerdp connects once you have creds.
